A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RNN learning-dynamics study. Their main text, equations, figures, and Appendices A-D support reliable comparison, including identification of the new appendix experiments and renumbered figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original RNN training simulations on double-integrator and multi-frequency tracking tasks, including learning curves, eigenspectra, and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original simulations and adds LQR-teacher and k-integrator experiments in Appendices A.5-A.6.

M1.justification: The Stage 2 surrogate optimized over order parameters changes: Eqs. 13-14 replace the t=3 short-term loss with a t=2 loss and remove the explicit T power on the long-term term. This modifies the surrogate optimization; the full RNN architecture and task-training objectives remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Appendix A.6 extends coverage to higher-order integrators, including k=3 and k=4, with varying actuation and partial versus full-state observations. This is a limited extension within the existing synthetic control domain; the original double-integrator and tracking tasks remain.

E2.justification: Figure 10 adds an open-loop student RNN supervised by an optimal LQR teacher as a comparator to closed-loop learning. v1's corresponding comparisons used an RNN teacher. The newly evaluated comparator is the LQR-trained student RNN.

E3.justification: The added LQR-teacher experiment trains on inputs from an LQR-controlled environment, whereas the original main-text open-loop experiment uses white-noise inputs. Figure 4d also changes the surrogate timestep and intermediate alpha values, with its color scale changing from 0.1-0.8 to 0.1-0.2. Original RNN training budgets are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix A.5 tests persistence of the transient loss peak with an alternative teacher and input-generation procedure. Appendix A.6 tests learning behavior across system orders, actuator counts, and observation conditions. These add targeted robustness checks while retaining the earlier regularization, optimizer, and representation analyses.

E5.justification: There are no added seed or repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The existing initialization comparisons and averaging of the cited human data remain unchanged.

E6.justification: New results show a transient peak with an LQR teacher, occasional open-loop non-convergence in partially observed k-integrators, and similar learning under tested full-state conditions. Some existing curves and example trajectories are revised, including Figs. 1c and 4d and v1 Fig. 17/v2 Fig. 19. The principal stage-wise and frequency-acquisition trends remain.

T1.justification: Appendices C.3-C.4 correct the determinant-lemma expression and define reduced coordinates as basis coefficients rather than simple inner products. C.6 generalizes the early-time loss to Lt, deriving t=1,2,3 cases and motivating t=2. A.6 defines the k-integrator family. The central spectral framework is retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and closing conclusion retain the same main contributions: different open- and closed-loop learning trajectories, competing short-term control and long-term stability objectives, and applicability to motor tracking. The added experiments support these retained claims.

C2.justification: Appendix A.6 adds an applicability qualification: the tested full-state configurations show similar learning in both regimes. Sections 4.1 and 6 strengthen the existing distinction between exact within-episode reduction and empirical agreement in learning behavior. Figure 4's caption also explicitly describes the validation as qualitative.

D1.justification: Appendix A.6 supplies explicit construction rules for the environment, actuator, and observation matrices and identifies tested configurations. A.5 documents LQR-controlled input generation. Existing training hyperparameters and the Python/PyTorch code-access statement are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Smekal et al., 'Towards a theory of learning dynamics in deep state space models,' as reference 52 in the discussion. Other reference changes primarily update existing works' bibliographic details; the overall research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites clarify the surrogate analysis and reduced-system interpretation, expand Appendix C.6, and introduce A.5-A.6. There are terminology corrections and a NeurIPS conference footer. The main section order and overall appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 10-11, revises Figure 4d and several captions or legends, and colors the appendix tracking outputs by frequency instead of training epoch. Most existing displays are retained with renumbering and modest page reflow.

improvement.justification: The additional control experiments strengthen validation and document full-state cases where the learning gap disappears. Corrected reduced-state coordinates, expanded loss derivations, and clearer limits on the reduction improve mathematical precision. These are limited gains to the retained study. The LQR experiment changes input generation as well as teacher, so it does not isolate teacher effects.
